source_review.notes: Checked all seven official/specification sources. Apache Avro 1.12 supports writer/reader schema resolution, defaults, aliases, unions, enums, and schema preservation claims. Current official Protocol Buffers proto3 guidance supports stable field-number and wire/JSON evolution distinctions. Current Confluent Schema Registry documentation supports backward/forward/full/transitive definitions, subject versions, and format-dependent rules. JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 supports dialect/vocabulary and additional-properties behavior. CloudEvents 1.0.2 specification/primer supports the separation of envelope specversion, type, dataschema, identity, and producer-owned payload versioning. Current Buf documentation supports distinct FILE/PACKAGE/WIRE_JSON/WIRE breaking-check scopes. Structural tool behavior is not elevated into domain-semantic proof.

evidence: Checked writer W_i, reader R_j, predicate C(R_j,W_i), coexistence/replay pair set P, retained writers H, active/candidate/rollback readers A, event identity m, event type tau, schema fingerprint s_i, and subject version v for consistent domains.
Confirmed compatibility quantifiers name the actual reader/writer direction and history set rather than relying on ambiguous labels.
Confirmed event type/schema changes are not conflated with subject-order or event-identity changes.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Compatibility predicate explicitly includes decode, structural, and declared semantic acceptability.

evidence: Recomputed four retained writer versions times four readers (two active, one candidate, one rollback) as 4*4=16 executable pairs.
Recomputed addition of one candidate writer as five writers times four readers, 5*4=20 pairs.
Confirmed backward candidate-reader coverage is four old-writer pairs and does not cover old readers against a new writer.
Counted ten worked examples and five exercise-answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Pair counts are exercise scenarios; real matrices also include languages, runtimes, encodings, rollback artifacts, and external consumers.

evidence: Expanded backward, forward, full, and transitive predicates and confirmed their stated reader/writer directions.
Constructed nontransitive v1-v2-v3 trace showing adjacent checks can pass while v3 reader fails retained v1 without a transitive check/upcaster.
Constructed structurally compatible numeric-unit change showing decode success does not imply semantic compatibility.
Constructed dual-publish trace showing two representations can create duplicate effects unless routing/shared effect identity is explicit.
Constructed mutable-registry-ID restore trace showing surviving event bytes are insufficient when writer schema resolution changes.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The safety argument depends on complete coexistence/replay inventory and evidence-preserving deterministic conversion.

evidence: Reviewed envelope specversion, media/serialization, event type/major, dataschema/fingerprint/registry ID, producer/consumer artifact, subject version, event ID, and routing epoch boundaries.
Reviewed Avro defaults/aliases/unions/enums/promotions, Protobuf numbers/unknown fields/enums/binary/JSON/source, and JSON open/closed objects/required/null/range/dialect behavior.
Reviewed units, timezone, identifier authority, null/unknown, precision, ordering/cardinality, snapshot/delta, finality, privacy, trigger, key, and causation semantics.

Reviewed rolling deployment/rollback, dormant consumers, multi-region caches, bridges, dual publication, upcaster purity/failure, archive replay, registry backup/delete/reuse, schema poisoning, and effect isolation.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans wire, structural, source, application, domain, temporal, operational, regional, replay, and adversarial boundaries.

evidence: Confirmed exact writer schema/original evidence remains resolvable throughout retention/replay and immutable schema identity is not reused.
Confirmed same event ID never names changed semantic content and subject version remains independent of schema/type version.
Confirmed every possible active/rollback/replay pair is covered by format-specific structural and semantic checks.
Confirmed upcasters are deterministic/pure, preserve identity/time/order/provenance, and represent unknown rather than invent current facts.
Confirmed breaking change creates explicit type/major/coexistence and retirement waits for observed consumers plus history/replay evidence.
invariant_checking.notes: Registry success is consistently treated as necessary structural evidence, not a complete compatibility certificate.

evidence: Reviewed compatibility-matrix proof and confirmed complete pair set, semantic invariance, and deterministic conversions are each necessary assumptions.
Reviewed defaults argument and confirmed read-time value cannot prove historical observation.
Reviewed rollback argument and confirmed already-emitted new writer data extends coexistence beyond deployment rollback.
Reviewed retirement argument and confirmed current traffic absence does not remove quarterly/archive/disaster consumers.
Reviewed upcaster argument and confirmed live I/O/clock/config makes historical interpretation nondeterministic.
proof_review.notes: Counterexamples prevent structural format rules from being generalized into unqualified event compatibility.

evidence: Confirmed proof sketch explicitly scopes its conclusion to the declared coexistence/replay matrix.
Confirmed Avro, Protobuf, Confluent, JSON Schema, CloudEvents, and Buf behaviors are attributed and version/configuration scoped.
Confirmed format requirements, registry enforcement, application design, semantic review, and empirical mixed-runtime verification are labeled separately.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Compatibility terminology is always paired with a concrete reader/writer sentence.

evidence: All seven official/specification references were retrieved or checked on 2026-09-02; Avro, JSON Schema, and CloudEvents references are version-pinned where applicable.
Example version counts, years, consumers, regions, and observation windows are labeled scenarios rather than universal policy.

Actual language/runtime serializer behavior, registry configuration/replication, consumer inventory, archived schemas, upcaster performance, semantic invariants, dual-publish parity, and retirement evidence remain explicit CI/integration/shadow/fault obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production registry, schema corpus, consumer fleet, archive, or event pipeline was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed version-dimension separation, compatibility matrices, Avro/Protobuf/JSON mechanics, semantic compatibility, strategy selection, upcasters/downcasters, mixed rollout, registry governance, history/replay, and verification as one event-lifecycle model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through named fields/fingerprints, format-specific CI/server gates, semantic checklists, immutable subjects, golden fixtures, pure upcasters, dual-write outbox identity, consumer-first rollout, rollback compatibility, registry/log backups, shadow parity, version telemetry, and evidence-based retirement.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module first disambiguates versions and compatibility directions, then teaches format mechanics, semantic review, migration mechanisms, rollout/governance, and historical replay. Ten examples isolate common evolution traps; five exercises progress from field taxonomy and matrix arithmetic through format review, upcaster design, and fleet migration with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
